# Unity Pipeline Program Charter v2.0

## ***\-\> Create Games Faster \<-***

## **Executive Summary**

### Create games faster

Unity Pipeline APIs reduce iteration time from minutes to seconds by opening up the Editor and pipeline to diverse personas—such as artists, QA, and producers—and by focusing on five key pillars:

* **Agentic Workflows:** Doubling down on the CLI to integrate AI agents directly into the game production process.  
* **Bridge Editor & Runtime:** Enabling direct-to-runtime workflows, live code iteration, and support for User Generated Content (UGC).  
* **Enhanced Collaboration:** Improving teamwork with features like "Play Scene" in the browser and Figma-like real-time collaboration.  
* **Open Ecosystem:** Introducing Pipeline APIs that allow for 1P, 2P, and 3P applications, turning production into a navigable, app-independent experience.  
* **API-First Approach:** Providing a robust foundation for custom tools, authentication, and role-based access control (RBAC).

**Impact**  
This platform shifts Unity productions away from the "problematic" bottleneck of requiring a single Editor seat for every interaction. By allowing diverse roles—from technical artists to stakeholders—to access project assets and perform reviews in context (web-based, desktop, or mobile), Unity Pipeline dramatically reduces handoff friction, on-boarding complexity, and operational costs.

**Strategic Trajectory**  
The roadmap targets General Availability by Q4 2026 (Unite Tokyo), moving toward an enterprise-ready, self-hosted deployment model by mid 2027, and integration with other Unity products like Studio by the end of 2027\.

## **Problem / vision**

It is tough to set up a Unity production environment where producers, artists, designers, external partners \- even automatic systems and AI Agents \- have efficient, concurrent and safe workflows. 

| The Unity Editor being the main entry point for everyone is problematic because workflows were never designed to support all these interactions simultaneously. In a macro-environment with constrained funding, this creates a negative \`perception about the value/cost of a Unity license:  Many team members don’t have the expertise to get valuable results out of the editor, The time it takes to onboard an internal or external collaborator is daunting, Teams have a limited ability to automate or extend tooling that scales reliably in production. | ![][image1] |
| :---- | :---- |

This pushes pipeline managers to conservatively restrict the number of editor licenses assigned across the team.

## **Unity Pipeline \- What is it?**

|  Unity Pipeline is a set of APIs and tools that open a Unity production beyond a single seat of the Editor. It allows studios to build an entire production pipeline from A to Z, for everyone on their team.  It decouples interactions from the Unity Editor, and defines a contract that allows interactions between people, software, agents and data.  | ![][image2] |
| :---- | :---: |

### What’s in the box

**Unity Pipeline is a set of APIs**, on which we’ve built features and tools to help customers build their pipelines:

- A [**Project Assets**](https://docs.unity.com/en-us/unity-production-pipeline/web-dashboard/get-started-web) section in the **dashboard** where you can see and navigate through project assets  
- [**CLI** & **pipeline package**](https://docs.unity.com/en-us/unity-cli) (**com.unity.pipeline**)  
  - Live Code Iteration?  
- A **Project API** that includes:  
  - **Workbench API** to interface with your Version Control System  
  - **Project Service** that produces artifacts for all assets in a workbench  
- [**Unity Version Control System**](https://unity.com/how-to/redeem/version-control)  
- [**Build automation**](https://docs.unity.com/en-us/oas-build-automation-client/2.0.0)  
  - **Build Accelerator** is a cache that speeds up build times  
- [**Pipeline automation**](https://docs.unity.com/en-us/cloud/automation)  
- [**Collaboration**](https://services.docs.unity.com/collaboration/v1/) service and Unity package (**com.unity.cloud.collaboration**) for annotations in and outside the editor  
- [**Deep linking service**](https://docs.unity.com/en-us/unity-production-pipeline/web-dashboard/deep-linking-web) & package (**com.unity.cloud.deep-linking** & **com.unity.cloud.authentication**)

### Project Service \- What is it?

Project Service is a backend implementation, **not a customer-facing component**. When a new asset is added to a workbench, the Project Service creates an on-demand (in seconds) Content File for this asset on the target platform.

### Pipeline Apps

On top of these APIs, the platform introduces the concept of **Pipeline apps**, and **context-aware links**.

* **A Pipeline app**: is any first, second, or third party tool that implements Pipeline APIs. It can be web-based, desktop, mobile, editor-integrated, or automated.  
* **A Pipeline link**: an app-independent URL allowing teams to move fluidly from one pipeline app to another, without losing context, reducing coordination cost and handoff friction.

**Unity Pipeline** turns Unity productions into an open, role-aware, and automatable pipeline ecosystem, rather than an editor-bound workflow. The platform connects four segments of content production users into a single, navigable ecosystem, offering role-specific user experiences through:

* **1P (first-party product**): An application developed and distributed by Unity requiring user seat entitlement, and billed with a mix of subscription/consumption.  
* **2P (second-party product)**: An application developed by a customer for their own needs, with our  APIs, requiring user/automation seat entitlement, and billed with a mix of subscription/consumption.  
* **3P (third-party product)**: An application developed by a customer that they monetize outside their organization, on top of our APIs, requiring user/automation seat entitlement, and billed with a mix of subscription/consumption.

## **North Star**

### Where are we heading in the long term?

**Unity Pipeline APIs and tools open a Unity production beyond a single seat of the Editor**, so the whole team, their tools and agents can work on the same projects. It aims to: 

* Reduce iteration time to seconds, not minutes  
* Allows **all users** in a studio to collaborate around a project  
* Allow multiple agents to iterate on projects, with a human-in-the-loop for verification  
* Requires no setup time  
* API first for enabling custom Apps

### Example workflows

These are example workflows of what we should be able to do with Unity Pipeline. This is not an exhaustive list. These are aspirational workflows, details and milestones will be gradual:

For User Story details, see [User Stories](?tab=t.m8u1b7gozqh2) sub-tab

**Creative Asset Iteration:** Artists, audio designers, and narrative designers modify assets or scenes (e.g., FBX, middleware sounds, dialogue strings) and verify changes immediately in-game on target devices.

**QA & Live Validation:** QA and automated systems test builds on devices, receiving live updates from developers to verify bug fixes and integration.

**Agentic Automation:** Developers delegate complex tasks to AI agents, such as investigating rare device bugs or executing parallel tasks across branches with automated side-by-side diffing.

**Custom Pipeline Development:** 2nd and 3rd-party developers build specialized, domain-specific "Editors" or web tools using Pipeline APIs, such as prefab-diff tools, custom level editors, game balancing dashboards, etc. 

**Real-Time Co-Editing:** Multiple team members and agents (e.g., environment artists and designers) work simultaneously on the same project branch, seeing each other's changes in real-time.

**Playtest & Stakeholder Review:** Game designers and producers distribute playable links for remote testing, allowing stakeholders to review work and leave in-context feedback.

**Cross-Platform Performance Analysis:** Technical artists run scenes across multiple target devices simultaneously to compare performance metrics against previous revisions.

**Governance & Access Control:** Producers manage project health, monitor branch status, and invite contractors with scoped access, all without needing an Editor seat.

**Build & Release Management:** Release engineers deploy content updates as independent artifacts, enabling rollbacks and content drops without rebuilding or redistributing the player binary.
